criteria.title: A mobility limitation stops a daily activity at home
criteria.requirement: A mobility examination documents a limitation that prevents the member from completing at least one daily activity in the home, such as toileting, dressing or preparing a meal.

criteria.title: A cane or walker does not resolve it
criteria.requirement: The examination states that a cane or a walker does not resolve the limitation.

criteria.title: A manual wheelchair does not resolve it
criteria.requirement: The examination states that the member cannot propel a manual wheelchair far enough to complete the daily activity.

criteria.title: The home accommodates the chair
criteria.requirement: A home assessment dated within the 60 days before the request confirms that doorways, turning space and floor surfaces accommodate a power wheelchair.

criteria.title: The member can operate it safely
criteria.requirement: The examination documents that the member has the vision, judgement and hand function to operate the controls safely.

evidence.text: Condition: G35.D Multiple sclerosis, unspecified. Onset 2009-02-14.

Clinical note (Mobility examination, dated 2026-09-05T12:00:00Z):
Face-to-face mobility examination, 2026-09-05.
She cannot get to the bathroom or prepare a meal without help.
A walker does not resolve the limitation; she stops after 10 feet.
She cannot self-propel a manual wheelchair more than 15 feet.
Her vision may be deteriorating; she was unsure of the joystick at first and I am not certain
she could stop reliably. Will reassess.

Clinical note (Home assessment, dated 2026-08-28T12:00:00Z):
Home assessment by the supplier, 2026-08-28.
Doorways 34 inches or wider, 5-foot turning space in the kitchen and bathroom, level vinyl floors,
ramp at the entrance. The home accommodates a power wheelchair.

value.rationale: The mobility examination documents that the member cannot get to the bathroom or prepare a meal without help, which constitutes a limitation preventing daily activities in the home.
The mobility examination explicitly states that a walker does not resolve the limitation.

The examination states that the member cannot self-propel a manual wheelchair more than 15 feet, which is insufficient to complete daily activities such as getting to the bathroom or preparing a meal.

The home assessment dated 2026-08-28 confirms that the home accommodates a power wheelchair. This date is within 60 days of the latest clinical note (2026-09-05), thus implying it would be within 60 days of a reasonable request date.

The examination raises concerns about the member's vision and judgment, stating she was unsure of the joystick and the clinician was 'not certain she could stop reliably,' indicating a lack of documentation that she can operate the controls safely.
